config.study_name: Northern Australia AI data-centre feasibility screening

connection._note: target_mw is the grid demand each network screen is tested against. It is set at or above the modelled peak facility demand (~244 MW for the training profile). reference_mw = 200 MW IT x base PUE 1.15, the value used in earlier versions of this study. load_trip_step_limit_percent is an initial-screening ASSUMPTION for the voltage-step limit (NER S5.1.5 voltage fluctuations and S5.3.7 fluctuating loads); it must be confirmed by Powerlink for the specific connection.

network_criteria._note: Planning assumptions. minimum_voltage_pu is the steady-state criterion; ner_minimum_load_pf are voltage-banded minimum load power factors adopted from NER S5.3.5 (verify against the current Rules version). The Pilbara is governed by the Pilbara Networks Rules; the same bands are applied there only for comparability.

water._note: Physics-based cooling-water estimate: evaporative heat rejection uses the latent heat of vaporisation plus blowdown at the given cycles of concentration. Below dry_cooling_limit_c all heat is rejected by dry coolers/economisers (no water); above full_evaporative_c it is fully evaporative; linear in between. Thresholds are design assumptions.

solar._note: pvlib single-axis tracking model. Capacities in the study are MW AC; dc_ac_ratio sets the DC array size. losses_fraction covers soiling, wiring, mismatch and availability (PVWatts default is ~0.14). irradiance_scale = 0.9 calibrates NASA POWER to metered output of three operating Central Queensland farms (mean metered/model ratio 0.89, run_solar_validation.py); 1.0 is kept as a sensitivity.

economics._note: Capital costs are CSIRO GenCost 2025-26 Final Report (July 2026), 2025 values: large-scale solar PV A$1,621/kW (Apx Table B.1); battery totals A$778/525/385/308 per kWh for 1/2/4/8 h (Apx Tables B.4-B.5), fitted as A$245/kWh + A$560/kW (within ~3% of all four). GenCost battery costs are on a usable-capacity basis. O&M values and the NWIS energy price are assumptions/placeholders.

network_tariff._note: Powerlink Transmission Shared Network Prices 2026/27 (GST inclusive; divided by 1.1 here). Node prices are published for the 132 kV nodes and are used as a proxy for a 275 kV connection. Locational price is applied to each month's peak grid import (simplification of Powerlink's billing basis); non-locational and common-service charges use the energy-based prices. Regulated connection charges are excluded. NWIS sites have no published equivalent and carry no network charge (flagged).

ppa._note: Optional renewable PPA hedge sensitivity: a fraction of annual grid energy is bought at a fixed price instead of spot. Price is a placeholder (VERIFY against current Queensland PPA market reports).

emissions._note: Location-based scope 2 factors, National Greenhouse Accounts Factors 2025 (DCCEEW), Table 1: Queensland 0.67, WA North Western Interconnected System 0.56 kg CO2-e/kWh.

scoring._note: Weights for the multi-criteria site comparison. water_use is the modelled cooling-water volume; water_score (supply security) and land_score (strategic industrial land) are 1-5 scores from cited public sources in candidate_sites.csv; hub_distance is the great-circle distance to the nearest major data-centre hub (a latency and fibre-route proxy). Criteria with no data for a site are excluded for all sites and the remaining weights renormalised.

dynamic_screening._note: Reduced-order dynamic screening following supervisor guidance: minimum and maximum operating conditions; sudden load pickup and loss; PV and BESS trip; network outage; voltage and frequency recovery. Voltage uses the Thevenin equivalent at each operating condition with a first-order voltage-control recovery. Frequency uses an aggregated swing-equation model with primary frequency response. System inertia, response and demand values are ASSUMED placeholders (VERIFY against AEMO inertia reports and Horizon Power/Pilbara ISO data); the robust outputs are the event size relative to the largest credible contingency and the minimum inertia/response each event needs. This is not a substitute for RMS/EMT studies in PowerFactory or PSS/E.

frequency_standard._note: NEM mainland Frequency Operating Standard, generation/load event row (AEMC Reliability Panel, effective 9 Oct 2023): containment 49.5-50.5 Hz, stabilisation 49.85-50.15 Hz within 5 minutes. The same bands are applied to the NWIS for comparison only (VERIFY against the Pilbara Networks Rules). RoCoF limit is an assumption.

NEM._note: largest_credible_contingency_mw = 750 MW (Kogan Creek, 710/750 MW summer/winter rating per Powerlink TAPR 2025 Table 6.1). Mainland inertia and response values are assumptions.

QLD_islanded._note: Queensland separated from NSW. Minimum inertia = AEMO 2024 Inertia Report Queensland minimum threshold level (12,000 MWs; secure level 13,700 MWs). Demand and frequency-response values remain assumptions. AEMO considers Queensland likely to island until QNI Connect is commissioned.

island_frequency_standard._note: NEM Frequency Operating Standard, island within the mainland, generation/load/network event: containment 49.0-51.0 Hz, stabilisation 49.5-50.5 Hz within 5 minutes (AEMO 2024 Inertia Report, Table 16).

growth_scenarios._note: Staged facility growth and declining system strength (e.g. coal retirement). Fault-level scale factors multiply the published minimum fault levels and are scenario assumptions, not forecasts.

oscillation_screening._note: AI training-load power oscillation screen based on Choukse et al. (2025, arXiv:2508.14318, Microsoft/NVIDIA production telemetry): swings occur 'once per second or less, to once every tens of seconds' with FFT energy at 0.2-3 Hz; GPUs exceed 50% of server power, so an unmitigated compute/communication swing is taken as ~50% of IT load; GB200 GPU power smoothing (power floor up to 90% of TDP) leaves ~10-20% dynamic range. Risky grid bands cited: ~0.16-2.5 Hz (line resonance, inter-plant oscillation) and 7-100 Hz (generator torsional modes). Pst for rectangular voltage changes uses the IEC 61000-4-15 Table 5 calibration points (VERIFY); planning levels from IEC 61000-3-7 / AS/NZS 61000.3.7.

price_aware_dispatch._note: Daily perfect-foresight linear programme (scipy HiGHS) minimising energy cost + network demand charge proxy + battery degradation, subject to the import limit. A benchmark for the best a price-aware controller could do; real controllers achieve less.

multibus._note: Reduced Central Queensland 275 kV equivalent. Topology and route lengths come from OpenStreetMap (build_cq_topology.py); circuit counts from Powerlink TAPR 2025 Appendix G and Chapter 6 where published, otherwise assumed (see branches.csv). Line impedance per km is typical for 275 kV; source impedances are fitted to the published minimum system-normal fault levels and validated against the published minimum N-1 values. Background flows and line ratings are not published, so results are incremental.

grid_section._note: Corridor-level thermal proxy for the Gladstone grid section (TAPR 2025 App. G: Bouldercombe into Calliope River, Raglan into Larcom Creek, Calvale into Wurdong; positive = into the Gladstone zone). The 2024/25 transfer duration curve is digitised by eye from TAPR 2025 Figure 6.17 (approximate, +/- ~30 MW). The effective limit is taken as the flow exceeded for the 54 constrained hours reported for 2024/25 (Section 6.6.4). Thermal ratings are dynamic and generation is re-dispatched when the section binds, so the result is an indication of added constraint hours, not a firm capacity.
grid_section.name: Gladstone

grid_emissions._note: Hourly Queensland generation-based emissions intensity built from AEMO Dispatch SCADA (5-min unit output for all scheduled and semi-scheduled units) and AEMO CDEII per-DUID CO2-e factors (NGA/ISP sourced). Interconnector flows are excluded (QLD is usually a net exporter). The most recent 365 days are converted to a month x hour-of-day x day-type profile and applied to every simulated hour, i.e. emissions reflect the current grid mix rather than the historical one.

solar_validation._note: Compare the pvlib model driven by NASA POWER with metered output of operating Central Queensland solar farms over the same months. Coordinates are approximate and single-axis tracking is assumed (VERIFY). AC capacity is estimated as the 99.5th percentile of hourly output; hours with QLD1 price <= 0 are excluded to remove economic curtailment.

cost_uncertainty._note: Latin-hypercube uncertainty over economic inputs for the primary site and import limit. Ranges are assumptions chosen to bracket published uncertainty (GenCost low/high ranges, recent price volatility); they are not probability distributions from data.

climate_scenarios._note: Uniform warming applied to dry-bulb and wet-bulb temperature of the 2020-2024 weather (a simple 'delta' method). Values bracket typical end-of-life (2050s) warming for northern Australia under medium-high emissions; VERIFY against CSIRO/BoM Climate Change in Australia projections for each region. Irradiance and wind are unchanged.

backup._note: Standby generation and reliability screen. All values are ASSUMPTIONS for screening (VERIFY): genset size and cost from typical large-data-centre practice, diesel properties from NGA (diesel ~38.6 GJ/kL, ~70.2 kg CO2-e/GJ => ~2.71 kg/L), outage statistics are placeholders to be replaced with Powerlink/Ergon reliability data for the connection point. The site BESS is also tested as a bridge.

rms_study._note: Open-source RMS dynamic study (ANDES) on the reduced Central Queensland 275 kV network (OSM topology, fitted line multiplier). Synchronous machines use GENROU with typical steam-unit parameters, TGOV1 governors (5% droop) and SEXS exciters; step-up transformers are neglected. Unit sizes per condition are chosen so total inertia matches AEMO's Queensland secure level (~13,000 MWs, minimum condition) or an interconnected NEM (maximum condition). Background loads are indicative zone loads (VERIFY: Powerlink zone forecasts / TAPR). All loads are constant power. This is an open-source substitute for, not a replacement of, PowerFactory/PSS/E studies with network-owner models.

hourly_flow._note: Hourly DC power flow on the multi-bus model for the most recent 365 days: Central Queensland unit output (AEMO Dispatch SCADA) injected at the mapped buses; background loads scaled with Queensland demand; the external system (fitted source impedances to a common reference) is the slack. Unit-to-bus mapping is by location (VERIFY: Powerlink connection points). Line ratings are not published: typical 275 kV ratings are assumed (VERIFY) and results are reported as loading relative to that assumption and as change caused by the data centre.

assumed_rating_mva._note: Typical summer rating of a single 275 kV twin-conductor circuit (VERIFY with Powerlink).

cq_sq_section._note: CQ-SQ crossing in the reduced model: circuits into Gin Gin plus Calvale's external equivalent (stands for Calvale-Halys). Duration curve digitised from Powerlink TAPR 2025 Figure 6.19 (2024/25); used only for validation.

hourly_flow._cases_note: Data-centre grid import held flat at the network target (245 MW, worst case) or at the 200 MW import limit that the on-site PV/battery design guarantees.

calibration._note: Two load multipliers fitted so the modelled Gladstone and CQ-SQ section duration curves (3-97% of time) match Powerlink's published 2024/25 curves; the indicative zone loads are otherwise unverified.

recent_prices._note: Prices after the 2020-2024 weather years, used only in run_recent_prices.py (2025 full year; 2026 to the latest published month).

rms_sensitivity._note: Extensions of the ANDES RMS study. (1) Frequency-response sensitivity for the Queensland-islanded minimum condition: system inertia, the share of the base governor response actually delivered (droop R / share; represents units without headroom, deadbands or not in frequency-response mode) and the governor valve time constant (6 s matches the reduced-order screen). (2) Fault ride-through: a near-bolted three-phase fault (0.005 pu, about 20,000 MVA, several times the published fault levels) at every bus, cleared in fault_clear_s; if the data-centre bus voltage falls below the assumed undervoltage trip threshold, the run is repeated with the whole facility disconnecting during the fault (Virginia-type event, NERC 2025). Trip threshold and clearing time are assumptions (VERIFY: facility UPS/protection settings; NER S5.1a.8 clearance times).

flexible_load._note: Demand flexibility of the training load (run_flexible_load.py). Pausing training saves energy and network cost but forgoes compute. Lost-compute value is the value of an IT MWh not delivered; it is swept because it depends on accelerator capital cost, utilisation and contract terms. Illustrative basis (VERIFY): ~A$6 bn of IT equipment for 200 MW of IT, 5-year life at 7% gives ~A$1.5 bn/yr, or ~A$850 per MWh of IT at full output. flexible_it_share is the share of IT that can be paused at short notice (checkpointed training jobs); the rest (inference, storage, networking) is firm.
